original_query: select  i_item_id,         s_state, grouping(s_state) g_state,         avg(ss_quantity) agg1,         avg(ss_list_price) agg2,         avg(ss_coupon_amt) agg3,         avg(ss_sales_price) agg4 from store_sales, customer_demographics, date_dim, store, item where ss_sold_date_sk = d_date_sk and       ss_item_sk = i_item_sk and       ss_store_sk = s_store_sk and       ss_cdemo_sk = cd_demo_sk and       cd_gender = 'F' and       cd_marital_status = 'D' and       cd_education_status = 'College' and       d_year = 1999 and       s_state = 'IN' and      i_category  = 'Electronics'  group by rollup (i_item_id, s_state)  order by i_item_id          ,s_state  limit 100;
rewritten_query:
SELECT i.i_item_id,
       s.s_state,
       GROUPING(s.s_state) AS g_state,
       AVG(ss.ss_quantity) AS agg1,
       AVG(ss.ss_list_price) AS agg2,
       AVG(ss.ss_coupon_amt) AS agg3,
       AVG(ss.ss_sales_price) AS agg4
FROM store_sales AS ss
JOIN customer_demographics AS cd
  ON ss.ss_cdemo_sk = cd.cd_demo_sk
JOIN date_dim AS d
  ON ss.ss_sold_date_sk = d.d_date_sk
JOIN store AS s
  ON ss.ss_store_sk = s.s_store_sk
JOIN item AS i
  ON ss.ss_item_sk = i.i_item_sk
WHERE cd.cd_gender = 'F'
  AND cd.cd_marital_status = 'D'
  AND cd.cd_education_status = 'College'
  AND d.d_year = 1999
  AND s.s_state = 'IN'
  AND i.i_category = 'Electronics'
GROUP BY ROLLUP (i.i_item_id, s.s_state)
ORDER BY i.i_item_id, s.s_state
LIMIT 100;

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: Rewrote implicit comma joins into explicit ANSI JOINs for readability and clearer join semantics; the planner sees the same plan, so no performance change expected.

All dimension filters (cd_gender='F', cd_marital_status='D', cd_education_status='College', d_year=1999, s_state='IN', i_category='Electronics') are simple constant predicates; no redundant predicates exist to remove.

This is a simple star join against one fact table with no repeated subquery calculations; no CTEs were introduced since inlining/materialization would not reduce work and could add overhead. The ROLLUP grouping is already handled efficiently with a single sort on i_item_id, so rewriting ROLLUP as GROUPING SETS or UNION ALL would add complexity with no gain.
Constant literals ('F', 'D', 'College', 1999, 'IN', 'Electronics', 100) are already in simplest form; no foldable expressions present.
